title: Is Luke Fickell back on the hot seat? Wisconsin collapse at Maryland renews questions
content:
Wisconsin’s fourth-quarter collapse in a 24-21 loss to Maryland will raise more doubts about whether Luke Fickell is the right person to continue leading the Badgers.

Fickell is in his fourth season at the helm, and after missing postseason play the last two seasons, Wisconsin (6-4, 4-3 Big Ten) became bowl eligible for the first time since 2023 with a win against Rutgers last week. Any momentum was halted Saturday with the loss at Maryland, which fired coach Mike Locksley four weeks ago and was playing without starting quarterback Malik Washington because of an injury.

The Terrapins (4-6, 2-5) rallied for 10 points in the final 2:11 to stun the Badgers and earn their second straight win under interim coach Aazaar Abdul-Rahim. Backup quarterback Cardell Williams completed 21 of 23 passes and accounted for three touchdowns, and the Terrapins held Wisconsin to just 201 total yards. Considering Maryland’s only Big Ten win last year came in a 27-10 thrashing at Wisconsin, Saturday’s result opens up speculation about Fickell, who falls to 23-25 in four seasons.

If new Wisconsin athletic director Shawn Eichorst makes a change after the season, the program would owe a buyout upward of $20 million, according to his contract. Eichorst’s history at Nebraska has shown he has no problems making such moves. Following the 2014 season, Eichorst fired then-Huskers head coach Bo Pelini following a 9-3 regular season. When asked if Nebraska’s overtime win in the finale at Iowa gave him pause, Eichorst said, “In the final analysis, I had to evaluate where Iowa was.”

With Fickell, that phrase once again could become applicable. Fickell is 0-4 against the Hawkeyes and has been outscored 109-10 the past three seasons. Two weeks ago, the Badgers lost 30-0 in Iowa City, one year after falling 37-0 at home. The Badgers also have lost two straight to their other rival, Minnesota.

The Badgers finish with a trip to Purdue, which they have beaten 18 straight times, and then at home against Minnesota. The outcomes of those contests likely will determine whether Fickell gets a reprieve or will be let go.
